home.keys: **J** **K** move through tasks · **↵** open · **E** done · **Esc** back here · **[** hide the list
home.setup.byom.title: Bring your own model
home.setup.byom.line: opencode’s free models run here for now: sign in to Claude Code, Codex or another, or add a key
home.setup.signin.title: Sign in to a coding agent
home.setup.signin.line: Use Claude Code, Codex or another you have, or start free with opencode’s models
home.setup.connect.title: Connect a coding agent
home.setup.connect.line: wisp drives Claude Code, Codex and more. No account? Start free with opencode’s models
home.setup.git.title: Install git
home.setup.git.line: Tasks get their own branch, and Ship it commits and pushes them, with git
home.setup.gh.title: Install the GitHub CLI
home.setup.gh.line: Ship it pushes your branch and opens the pull request with gh
home.setup.ghIn.title: Sign in to GitHub
home.setup.ghIn.line: So tasks can push their branch and open a pull request when you ship them
home.setup.gridHere.title: Reach this wisp from anywhere
home.setup.gridHere.line: Put this computer on a wisp Grid and open it at your grid address from your phone or any browser. No SSH, no open ports
home.setup.gridOn.title: This wisp opens from anywhere
home.setup.gridOn.line: It lives at {address}: open it from your phone, another computer or any browser, signed in with this account
home.install.line: No coding agent here yet. opencode runs free models, no account needed.
home.install.busy: Installing opencode into ~/.wisp/tools… usually under a minute
home.install.ready: {name} is ready: free models, no account needed. Type a task and press Enter.
home.install.still: Still no harness found. Install opencode here, or Claude Code, Codex, Cursor… yourself. The ChatGPT app (Codex) or the Claude app (its Code tab) works too.
home.ios.install: Add wisp to your Home Screen: tap Share, then Add to Home Screen
home.getapp.title: wisp for your desktop
home.getapp.why.notify: Notifications when an agent needs you, with no tab to keep open
home.getapp.why.editor: Opens files in your editor and your terminal in one click
home.getapp.why.grid: Your agents on your own computer too, and this cloud computer right next to them
home.getapp.why.window: Its own window and Dock icon, a folder picker, and it starts with your computer
home.getapp.hidden: Hidden. Search (⌘K) still has Get the desktop app.
home.notify.question: {title} has a question
home.overlap.clean: Also changes {files}, but they merge cleanly
home.overlap.allTitle: All the tasks that change the same files
home.overlap.dialog.one: Changes the same files as 1 task
home.overlap.dialog.other: Changes the same files as {count} tasks
home.overlap.hint: Only tasks in Working or Needs you count.
home.overlap.hintClash.one: 1 would conflict if both were merged. Only tasks in Working or Needs you count.
home.overlap.hintClash.other: {count} would conflict if both were merged. Only tasks in Working or Needs you count.
home.signin.sending: Signed in. Sending your request again…
home.signin.oldCli: Claude Code before 2.1.318 can stop other running tasks on this login when you sign in. Update it first if you have tasks running.
home.signin.title: {agent} is signed out
home.watch.title: Watch
home.watch.local: This points at the agent’s computer; it may not load here.
home.waiting: Waiting for a computer: tasks you start now go when it’s back
home.tip.goal: Turn on **Goal**, say when it’s done, and wisp sends the task back each round until it holds
home.tip.goalCmd: Type **/goal** in a reply box to keep a task going until your condition holds
home.tip.vs: Click **vs** in the launcher to run the same task on two agents, each on its own branch
home.tip.compare: **Compare** lines runs up side by side: time, cost, tests and the diff. **Keep this** keeps the winner
home.tip.auto: Leave the harness on **Auto** and wisp picks the agent and model per task from what worked for you
home.tip.limit: When Claude Code hits its usage limit, Auto rests it and hands the next tasks to another agent
home.tip.worktrees: Every task gets its own git worktree and branch, so parallel agents never touch the same files
home.tip.keyN: Press `N`, describe a task, Enter, and the next one: launch tasks back to back
home.tip.keyT: Press `T` on a task to take it over in your own terminal, in its worktree
home.tip.ship: **Ship it** commits, pushes and opens the PR; **Merge** squash-merges and syncs your local main
home.tip.delegate: Give one agent a team: **Delegate** lets a Claude Code lead hand work to Codex copies in parallel
home.tip.delegateMachine: **Delegate** can put a member on another machine: the lead hands it work there and gets the changes back
home.tip.preset: **Save as preset** in Delegate keeps a team for the next big task
home.tip.mcp: Add `wisp mcp` to the agent in your editor and it can launch and wait on wisp tasks
home.tip.runOn: **Run on** next to the harness sends one prompt to several machines at once
home.tip.machines: **Machines** connects any computer you can SSH into: a desktop, a dev box, a cloud VM
home.tip.battery: Laptop battery low? **Runs on** by the follow-up box moves the task, branch and history to another computer
home.tip.switch: Stuck agent? Switch the harness in the follow-up box and Codex picks up where Claude Code stopped
home.tip.rerun: **Rerun** can start a task over on another machine or with another agent
home.tip.tailscale: Tailscale makes your machines reachable from anywhere, phone included, with nothing exposed
home.tip.phone: Reach this computer from your phone: **Machines** → _Reach this computer from anywhere_
home.tip.laptop: Close the laptop: tasks on wisp Cloud or another machine keep working
home.tip.cloud: wisp Cloud gives you a box with Claude Code, Codex and Cursor installed, free during the preview
home.tip.modes: Pick **Plan** for read-only, **Edits** to approve commands, or **Full auto**, per task
home.tip.away: Questions and finished tasks can go to your phone through ntfy or Telegram
home.tip.btw: `/btw` asks a running agent something without interrupting it
home.tip.recipes: **Recipes** are saved prompts with `{params}`: one click for the tasks you repeat
home.tip.triggers: **Triggers** run a recipe on a schedule, when CI fails, or when an issue gets a label
home.tip.checkpoints: Every turn is checkpointed in its worktree, so you can roll an agent’s work back
home.tip.cli: `wisp "fix the flaky test" --wait --json` runs a task from a script and waits for it
home.tip.api: Webhooks, a JS SDK and an HTTP API let your own tools start tasks and read reports
home.tip.spell: Type `/spell` and describe a change: wisp builds it into itself, and you try it first
home.tip.spells: Spells add buttons, panels, chips and commands, restyle wisp, or hide what you don’t use
home.tip.share: Share a spell with your team as one file or one link
home.tip.safe: wisp looks odd? Settings → Spells → _Turn every spell off_, or start with `WISP_SAFE=1`
home.tip.harnesses: wisp runs Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, opencode, Antigravity, Grok and Copilot CLIs you already have
home.tip.grid: Run your own wisp Grid for your team: sign-in, a sandbox each, on one server
home.tip.accounts: Have a work and a personal Claude plan? Add the other in Settings → Agents and pick one per task
home.tip.accountLimit: At an account’s limit the task asks what to do; wisp never switches accounts for you
home.tip.p.cloud: **Cloud** is your wisp on a server: its agents keep working with every computer switched off
home.tip.p.computer: **Your computer** opens while it’s awake: tasks there run on its own files, repos and tools
home.tip.p.lock: Lock the phone or switch apps: tasks run on the computer, not here, and wait for you when they ask
home.tip.p.newTask: **New task** starts one on any of your computers; the **wisp logo** brings you back to the list
home.tip.p.needs: Questions from your agents show under **Needs you**: answer from here and the task picks up
home.tip.p.swipe: Swipe a task right to mark it done, left to save it for later; each comes with **Undo**
home.tip.p.auto: Leave the agent on **Auto** and wisp picks the agent and model per task from what worked for you
home.tip.p.parallel: Start several tasks at once: each gets its own branch, so agents never touch the same files
home.tip.p.goal: Turn on **Goal** and a task keeps going round after round until your check passes
home.tip.p.ship: **Ship it** commits, pushes and opens the pull request, right from your phone
home.tip.p.signedIn: Signed in to Claude Code or Codex on that computer? The phone uses them as they are
home.tip.p.private: No ports to open: the grid carries your tasks to you, while your files and logins stay on the computer
